text:
Matthew Knies said before the game that coming back to Toronto "feels a little awkward." By the end of the night it was the Maple Leafs who looked uncomfortable. Knies, traded to Columbus for Kirill Marchenko in late September, tied the game with 4:20 left, Zach Werenski won it 52 seconds later, and the Blue Jackets beat the Leafs 4-3 after trailing by two. Toronto is now winless in nine (0-8-1).

The Leafs did a lot right early. Auston Matthews scored on the power play late in the first, and after Damon Severson tied it with 17 seconds left in the period, Jake McCabe put Toronto back ahead with five seconds to go on a shot our numbers gave a 4% chance. Teddy Blueger made it 3-1 early in the second. Cam Talbot kept the gap from getting bigger, stopping Darren Raddysh on a 35% chance in the first.

Columbus never stopped coming. The Blue Jackets out-attempted Toronto 78 to 49 and outshot them 35 to 26, and Adam Fantilli's power-play goal in the second cut it to 3-2. Knies' tying goal, unassisted, lifted Columbus' win chances from 11% to 48%; Werenski's backhand, set up by Fantilli, took them to 90%. Werenski played 32 minutes, and Knies was on the ice for 0.23 expected goals against (the quality of the chances allowed) in 21 and a half minutes. Anthony Stolarz allowed a goal more than his shots deserved, and our replays gave Columbus the win 55% of the time.

The reaction in Toronto was loud. The Leafs Nation reported "Fire Hiller" chants after the third-period collapse, aimed at Jim Hiller, hired in June. Matthews called the loss "inexcusable," and Daily Faceoff carried his line: "We should be embarrassed." With his own name in trade speculation headlines this month, along with William Nylander's, that is the captain describing a team in real trouble a quarter into the season.

For Columbus, it was a night to enjoy. Werenski has spent the season answering questions about his future during a rough start, and this win came with him on the ice for 2.44 expected goals for. Toronto won the first meeting 6-2 in October. The second one will be remembered for who scored the tying goal.
headline: Knies comes home and helps sink the Leafs again
